findings.title: Feature-enabled dashboard tables discard all query results
findings.description: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, every table receives empty columns, rows, and metadata instead of the current `result`. Consequently, populated dashboard widgets become empty tables. Pass the actual query results and configured columns to `TableWidgetVisualization`, or retain the existing renderer until the integration is complete. Add a widget-level test with the flag enabled and nonempty results.

findings.title: Attribute-key cache identity omits the organization
findings.description: The new query key contains only a constant and query options, but `useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys` fetches an organization-specific URL. Two organizations with identical filters—for example, an empty project selection or `[-1]`—therefore share a cache entry. Switching organizations can temporarily display the previous organization’s custom attribute names. Include the organization slug or complete endpoint URL in the query key, and test switching organizations with unchanged filters.

findings.title: Replay errors and recording events use different timestamp units
findings.description: The merge compares nodestore error timestamps directly with recording-event timestamps. Error timestamps are epoch seconds, as confirmed by `BaseEvent.datetime`, whereas raw replay recording timestamps use milliseconds, including examples in `tests/sentry/replays/unit/test_event_parser.py`. With real timestamps, errors are emitted before the first recording event regardless of their actual occurrence time, undermining the chronological context supplied to the summary. Normalize both sources to the same unit and test realistic epoch timestamps.

findings.title: Error messages are read from the wrong nodestore field
findings.description: `nodestore.backend.get_multi()` returns raw stored event dictionaries, whose normalized message lives under `logentry.formatted` or `logentry.message`, not the top-level `message` field. `BaseEvent.message` explicitly handles this distinction. As written, message-only errors lose their message context, and exception details not represented in the stored title are omitted. Construct `Event` objects from the fetched data and use their title/message accessors, or extract the normalized fields explicitly. Cover a stored logentry-based error in the tests.

findings.title: Custom table renderers cannot intentionally return empty content
findings.description: The truthiness check treats valid renderer results such as `null`, `false`, `''`, and `0` as requests to run the fallback renderer. This prevents callers from intentionally hiding a cell and replaces a custom zero value with the default rendering. The header renderer has the same issue. Since the documented fallback sentinel is `undefined`, use `cell !== undefined` in both renderers and add tests for empty and zero-valued custom results.
